comments.body: I mounted the second GPU into a docker container allowing it to masquerade as a single GPU and when directing OVMS docker image built from source with GPU permissions it loaded correctly into the second GPU alone The moment another GPU is mounted within the container the script fails to load a model into the secondary GPU OpenVINO and thus OpenVINO model server has a serious issue of not being able to target secondary GPUs in environments completely breaking multi gpu configs and HETERO configs

comments.body: Hi ligjn It looks like you have downloaded the model manually OVMS needs a graph pbtxt file for llm models to work in the model directory You can create one manually or you can use the automatic graph pbtxt file creation with the ovms pull functionality To use it make sure the models OpenVINO TinyLlama 1 1B Chat v1 0 int8 ov directory does not exist on you local filesystem Then run the command ovms pull model repository path models source model OpenVINO TinyLlama 1 1B Chat v1 0 int8 ov task text generation This will pull the model You can review the required graph pbtxt file in models OpenVINO TinyLlama 1 1B Chat v1 0 int8 ov graph pbtxt Alternatively if you want to serve one model without the config you can run the pull and start mode for ovms with this command ovms model repository path models source model OpenVINO TinyLlama 1 1B Chat v1 0 int8 ov task text generation rest port 8000 Or you can add the downloaded model to config file with this command ovms add to config models model name OpenVINO TinyLlama 1 1B Chat v1 0 int8 ov model path OpenVINO TinyLlama 1 1B Chat v1 0 int8 ov And start ovms as you have done it with ovms config path models config json rest port 8000 log level DEBUG

title: /metrics endpoint bad content-type
body: Describe the bug The metrics endpoints uses content type application json while Prometheus v3 expects e g plain text curl head http 10 42 0 72 8000 metrics HTTP 1 1 200 OK content length 14299 content type application json charset utf 8 access control allow headers access control allow methods access control allow origin Prometheus throws Error scraping target received unsupported Content Type application json charset utf 8 and no fallback scrape protocol specified for target img width 1912 height 362 alt Image src https github com user attachments assets a65e5ab8 5573 408b bb7b ab4dc3f7f58f Seems like Prometheus v2 quietly tolerated this and v3 is more strict See https prometheus io docs prometheus latest migration scrape protocols https prometheus io docs prometheus latest migration scrape protocols Workaround Explicitly set fallbackScrapeProtocol in a ScrapeConfig for OVMS To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior 1 Run OVMS with metrics enable and rest port 8000 2 Setup Prometheus v3 to scrape the metrics endpoint Expected behavior metrics endpoint uses correct content type in header Configuration 1 OVMS version 4 0 0 2 Prometheus v3 My setup was k3s with prometheus community kube prometheus stack https github com prometheus community helm charts tree main charts kube prometheus stack and OVMS installed via Helm https github com openvinotoolkit operator tree main helm charts ovms https github com openvinotoolkit operator tree main helm charts ovms

title: installing the ovms binary deployment on Ubuntu 24.04
body: The installation steps in the official documentation are as follows img width 1462 height 865 alt Image src https github com user attachments assets a376b41e 994a 415a 8d42 36fa0dd0017d There is a problem here the Python installed via apt is global which will affect the machine s original Python environment Ideally shouldn t the OVMS installation package include its own Python environment just like the Windows version so that it doesn t affect the machine s own environment At the same time on a clean Ubuntu 24 04 machine it is impossible to complete the installation by following the official documentation exactly img width 1892 height 380 alt Image src https github com user attachments assets 0dc84664 5ee2 47da a106 1cb0a1c251a6 I understand that it might be necessary to add the break system packages parameter but this seems unreasonable Could you provide a self contained Python environment similar to the Windows version

title: Usage of HETERO to split models among multiple devices results in garbled outputs at long context.
body: Introduction After playing around extensively with OVMS in single and multi HETERO GPU configurations with a variety of models Qwen3 32B 14B 8B Llama3 8B bge m3 and bge reranker v3 I ve come to the conclusion that there may be an issue with processing long context situations on HETERO devices To come to the conclusion that I have that HETERO devices has issues at long contexts I would put each of the following configs through the same 3 tests 1 Sending a brief message to assess whether the model had loaded properly and was responding at acceptable speeds and with relative accuracy Tell me about yourself in brief detail 2 Injecting a 3 page document 1600 words which is embedded using OVMS BAAI bge m3 with the prompt Summarise this document in 4 5 key points The entire document is loaded into context 3 Injecting a 17 page document 8700 words which is embedded using OVMS BAAI bge m3 with the prompt Summarise this document in 4 5 key points This entire document is loaded into context Please note that when mention is made of Qwen3 models I had specifically disabled thinking adding no think in the system prompt and was using the recommended model params from Qwen s model card with regards to non thinking prompts Also note that the embedding model is loaded into a third seperate GPU GPU 2 not used in the HETERO config Also note that when a test case is deemed as a FAIL it means the model gave an OOM error and no further prompts could be sent to that model Context excuse the pun 1 Qwen3 14B in GPU 0 Quantisation command python export model py text generation source model Qwen Qwen3 14B weight format int4 config file path media models config json overwrite models target device GPU 0 model repository path media models tools model type qwen3 cache size 6 extra quantization params awq dataset wikitext2 ratio 0 8 group size 64 kv cache precision u8 When working initially with OVMS I experimented with Qwen3 14B as when quantised to INT4 it would seemingly fit into a single GPUs VRAM This had added benefits as it was no longer dealing with splitting the model and its smaller size meant it responded extremely quickly to prompts be they big or small Test cases 1 PASS with good accuracy 2 PASS with good accuracy 3 PASS with good accuracy This model performs extremely well There are some things to note though The VRAM from context doesn t seem to clear itself which means that it can sometimes OOM after multiple followup prompts I haven t experienced this recently but it was an issue earlier on 2 Qwen3 32B in HETERO GPU 0 GPU 1 This section will be split into three subsections as there have been multiple attempts at using this model each with their own intricacies that may be relevant or not to the development team of OVMS There is one thing that does need to be noted here and that is the usage of kv cache precision u8 The addition of this flag to any of the export model py quantisations results in a HUGE slowdown in model performance and usually leads to OOM errors even though this shouldn t happen On its own this is a huge issue and not one that is present on single GPU loading models like Qwen3 14B above Without u8 precision in the KV Cache context fills up extremely quickly and more often leads to OOM errors Interestingly enough you can change the cache size with Qwen3 14B to something smaller than 10 as seen above where we set it to 6 and OOM errors do not usually crop up but limiting the cache size with Qwen3 32B almost ALWAYS results in problems with the model 2 1 INT 4 Quantization no extra params Quantization command python export model py text generation source model Qwen Qwen3 32B weight format int4 config file path media models config json overwrite models target device HETERO GPU 0 GPU 1 model repository path media models tools model type qwen3 This config worked initially however fell apart fast Small prompts would yield fast responses and accurate results but the moment you start putting more into the model its grammar falls apart It is almost as if it lost the ability to use connective words like to the then etc Test cases 1 PASS with good accuracy but fail on follow ups 2 PASS with terrible accuracy response falls apart 3 PASS with terrible accuracy response falls apart This configuration of Qwen3 32B performs horribly with response quality indicating that strictly quantising the model down to INT4 yields accuracy errors and obliterates the models ability to converse with the user 2 2 INT 4 Quantization extra params AWQ DATASET and SCALE ESTIMATION Quantisation command python export model py text generation source model Qwen Qwen3 32B weight format int4 config file path media models config json overwrite models target device HETERO GPU 0 GPU 1 model repository path media models cache size 10 tools model type qwen3 extra quantization params ratio 0 8 group size 64 awq dataset wikitext2 scale estimation pipeline type LM disable dynamic split fuse A note on this command The addition of dataset and scale estimation renders strange results Occasionally these commands will end up with a working model but most of the time the model will fail to export properly The only thing I ve noticed is that every now and again completely deleting the wikitext2 dataset from the HF cache and having the command redownload it results in a working model for that specific SSH session but any further attempts to use it in other SSH sessions fail The addition of these extra params also causes the model to time out on the third test More on that later When this config works it works But 90 of the time it doesn t due to the problems mentioned above with the addition of the extra params However the addition of these params although it s my suspicion that at minimum it s the addition of awq the models responses clean up extremely well and accuracy is restored Test cases 1 PASS with good accuracy 2 PASS with good accuracy 3 FAIL Unfortunately as mentioned above the addition of the extra params which is limited down to dataset and scale estimation as shown below results in the model completely timing out and erroring due to OOM Out of resources 2 3 INT 4 Quantization extra params AWQ Quantization command python export model py text generation source model Qwen Qwen3 32B weight format int4 config file path media models config json overwrite models target device HETERO GPU 0 GPU 1 model repository path media models cache size 10 tools model type qwen3 extra quantization params ratio 0 8 group size 64 awq pipeline type LM disable dynamic split fuse A note on this command This command is the most reliable one I ve used so far and always results in a usable model In fact if I wasn t trying to identify WHY long context breaks the model and was just using it with the embedding an reranking workflows I usually use I wouldn t be making this issue Alas though taking this as a problem that doesn t occur just because you don t push the model further enough isn t good enough and it s edge cases like these that take a project like model server from good to fantastic This configuration works fantastic almost always leading to fantastic responses with good token generation speeds even with larger context windows like the ones seen in test 2 As mentioned above this would be perfect if it wasn t for test case 3 Test cases 1 PASS with good accuracy 2 PASS with good accuracy 3 PASS with Chinese characters which really means it s a fail Unfortunately test case 3 is where this config falls apart The model succeeds in responding and successfully load balances the KV cache which the previous configuration with params did not and while the response speed is slow which it s meant to be for long context the response is all in Chinese In fact it s all in two to three Chinese characters on loop sometimes starting with a number like 1 or 4 This is not unheard of in fact there are other implementations of Qwen3 that do this same thing or used to from memory llama cpp did this at the start with Qwen models until the chat template was fixed If I had to guess this is a small problem with the way the model is quantised but could also be a model server implementation problem Conclusion OVMS seems to have been a project focused on smaller models in the past with many benchmarks and use cases being for models under 8B params However with the addition of the HETERO config it seems that it s wanting to push further into using larger models Personally I think larger models like Qwen3 32B are exactly what the open source community need to push back against giants like OpenAI and I myself am in huge support of projects like OVMS I am in awe of the performance not only in token generation but also in TTFT that this project has achieved and hope that my findings with the HETERO config can help to patch up more bugs that might be hanging around If there is anything else I can do to help identify what might be happening here please don t hesitate to leave a comment I m happy to test anything Edit I ve since played around with this further and found that the limit for text input seems to be between 4 5 thousand words When initially ingesting using the working quantization method above for 32B it doesn t want to overflow it s KV cache into the second GPU and seems to stall endlessly

comments.body: I wish to make a followup to this post to detail some further findings I ve had It seems that OVMS was running into resource issues and not allocating things correctly to GPUs since the quantisation commands for HETERO specified that I must use pipeline type LM HOWEVER The mainline OpenVINO patched HETERO devices to support continuous batching in July so building OVMS with python support and using the latest builds from OpenVINO OpenVINO GenAI and other respective projects while also modifying the export model py script to remove the barriers on setting LM CB pipeline type when quantising results in Qwen3 32B working PERFECTLY at extremely large contexts For all those who encounter this issue using HETERO configs in the future please note that doing the same modifications will result in an extremely performant model with limited accuracy issues The one thing to note is that once you modify the export model py script you ll need to add tools model type qwen3 and extra quantization params awq group size 128 to the default command otherwise you will run into accuracy issues I have found that data free AWQ seems to clean up a lot of issues with Qwen3 Thank you

title: Missing /v3/models endpoint
body: Describe the bug The OpenAI API has a models endpoint https platform openai com docs api reference models The API docs describe it as List and describe the various models available in the API You can refer to the Models docs models documentation to understand what models are available and the differences between them Lists the currently available models and provides basic information about each one such as the owner and availability Example query curl https api openai com v1 models H Authorization Bearer OPENAI API KEY And there is a models model for Retrieves a model instance providing basic information about the model such as the owner and permissioning OVMS does not currently implement this endpoint returning an error when one tries to access it curl http localhost 8080 v3 models error Invalid request URL Some tools like Open WebUI uses the models endpoint to discover available models when a new connection is configured Because this endpoint fails one needs to manually enter the model name This name is not always a well known string and it needs to be found in the OVMS config command or logs OVMS already has a similar enpoint under v1 config which lists the served model s which is not under the OpenAI base path and does not follow the OpenAI format The comonly used OpenAI compatible clients can therefore not use it Because the information is available it seems to be possible to expose it also under v3 models in the correct format Configuration 1 OVMS version v2025 2 1

body: Describe the bug Because OVMS does not support CORS https developer mozilla org en US docs Glossary CORS it is impossible to use it directly from a web browser via a Web client such as OpenWebUI https openwebui com This is a missing OVMS feature seen as a bug from the client s perspective Feel free to remove the bug label The web browser denies the requests when the server fails to respond to the preflight request https developer mozilla org en US docs Glossary Preflight request Access to fetch at http localhost 8081 v3 chat completions from origin http localhost 8080 has been blocked by CORS policy Response to preflight request doesn t pass access control check No Access Control Allow Origin header is present on the requested resource If an opaque response serves your needs set the request s mode to no cors to fetch the resource with CORS disabled In the above case the Web UI at origin http localhost 8080 is denied access to OVMS at http localhost 8081 by the browser Moreover the responses don t include any of the CORS headers https developer mozilla org en US docs Glossary CORS cors headers To Reproduce 1 Run OpenWebUI 2 Configure a direct connection Use http localhost title: When inferencing tokenizer model, special tokens are not automatically added.

title: Using Go KServer API request inferred, OVMS crashes abnormally
body: Describe the bug When using the Go Kserver API to access the Text to Image service provided by ovms the OVMS service crashes abnormally which is more like the program being killed directly To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior My OVMS version 2025 0 My startup command ovms exe port 9000 config path config json log level DEBUG Image https github com user attachments assets 7c2b1c74 c4be 4641 bfcf aea1cdfd4a64 Image https github com user attachments assets f280d049 4150 413c abb8 0e31e93286d7 My graph pbtxt and python code Image https github com user attachments assets 5bc20d78 ba60 4091 8c1d 406ebb1fab40 Image https github com user attachments assets 5da8e752 15ca 4946 8acb cc30f0510add I use the Python Kserver api call and the service can respond and return normally but I use the Go Kserver api call and the service crashes abnormally Python Code Image https github com user attachments assets 468a26bb 951a 4807 a038 bd6e0ed0b0f0 Request Image https github com user attachments assets 1faa2e40 89ee 4838 9212 c1e3e867bf2a Result Image https github com user attachments assets 77094095 50e8 4839 b262 6f0cc4244f61 Go Both Live Ready Kserver APIs can respond normally but requesting the Text to Image service will cause OVMS to crash abnormally Code Image https github com user attachments assets 1803c9ac bb21 43c7 9b61 c61efc73b59f Result Image https github com user attachments assets ebfc94be 9951 4eb4 8f76 30d4e11f5135 Image https github com user attachments assets debb2936 171d 4ed7 8fdf f4c8055935c7 Why is the OVMS process being obscured and not getting any useful information I really hope to get your help Thanks

comments.body: Hi ligjn from the printing you have in the Python code looks like the crash happened along with generation call to GenAI pipeline To make sure this is the case could you also add print after generate call Also could you check if the same happens if you change device to CPU Since it s the client that makes a difference I suspect the data received on the server side is different so pipeline gets different input that inference plugin might have problem with

mzegla As can be seen in the figure below the device is modified to the CPU Before running self pipe generate on line 26 there is a printing input information and after running there is also an operation to print End execute The following is the actual executed python code Image https github com user attachments assets 9a988c26 9461 44f8 b7a9 49dcac801399 Python Result Image https github com user attachments assets 185ff68d 119f 49d3 88ee e54aa2c0bc4a Ovms log Image https github com user attachments assets a1e18a81 d341 49ca aaff 1884ef965494 Go Result Image https github com user attachments assets fe594369 44ac 4ef0 b77d 4a63d8373bd6 Ovms log Image https github com user attachments assets 6f8469ba c3d1 44e0 a32d 669bc03a6a17 As can be seen from the above performance in the case of the two inputs are exactly the same Go client side access after executing to self pipe generate ovms crashed directly which is what I don t understand Even if self pipe generate fails to execute ovms should not crash directly causing all other model services to hang up Hope to get your reply thank you

comments.body: sriram dsl Duplicating the models is not the recommended method for scalability and multi concurrency Nireq parameter is also not causing the parallel processing it is a size of the queue of the requests If you have just one model and you want to optimized for processing 4 concurrent requests you should increase the number of streams in the model and use just one model Set parameter NUM STREAMS If you have 4 clients probably two streams will be optimal That depends how long the client is processing the response and how long it is sending the requests It is likely that one synchronous client will not be able to fully utilized one stream Try setting four streams to confirm Nireq is by default equal to the number of streams which is usually sufficient You can increase it but it shouldn t be lower Note that increasing the number of streams will improve the throughput for most of the models but it will also impact the latency Single stream will have divided resources available for computing In case you have 4 completely different models the recommendations are different because the streams are managed in the scope of a single model With multiple models you should use just one stream in each model default setting and reserve the resources for each model There are special parameters which can reserve and pin individual cores to each model Consider this config json json model config list config name model1 base path model resnet 50 tf plugin config INFERENCE NUM THREADS 2 ENABLE CPU RESERVATION true ENABLE CPU PINNING true config name model2 base path model resnet 50 tf plugin config INFERENCE NUM THREADS 2 ENABLE CPU RESERVATION true ENABLE CPU PINNING true config name model3 base path model resnet 50 tf plugin config INFERENCE NUM THREADS 2 ENABLE CPU RESERVATION true ENABLE CPU PINNING true It will assign 2 different cpu cores to each model It will ensure that execution on one model is not impacting the rest

How can I measure throughput effectively Is there a tool similar to NVIDIA s perf analyzer that I can use for this purpose Additionally if I deploy a container within a Kubernetes cluster to enable scaling how can I scale the models running inside each container

sriram dsl you can use perf analyser Kserve API in OVMS is compatible with Triton so the same benchmarking tool can be used You can use also this tool https github com openvinotoolkit model server tree main demos benchmark python In Kubernetes you can enable horizontal autoscaling to tune the number of replicas depending on the load If can you prefer to deploy just a single container you can scale the container vertically by adding more resources In can you want to optimize for best throughput results add in the plugin config PERFORMANCE HINT THROUGHPUT If you want to optimize for latency set PERFORMANCE HINT LATENCY

title: [Bug]: OpenVINO Server does not override the default max_context_length=512 with the value specified in the model.xml file
body: OpenVINO Version 2024 5 Operating System Windows 11 Device used for inference GPU Framework None Model used BAAI bge m3 Issue description Openvino Server does not override the default max context length 512 with the one contained in the model xml file Step by step reproduction Convert the embedding model to the OpenVINO IR format using the OpenVINO Toolkit and serve it with the openvino model server latest gpu Docker image When calling the http localhost 8001 v3 embeddings API the server throws the following error even though the model has a max position embeddings value of 8194 calculator graph cc 853 INVALID ARGUMENT CalculatorGraph Run failed in Run Calculator Process for node EmbeddingsCalculator failed Input length 617 longer than allowed 512 Relevant log output shell calculator graph cc 853 INVALID ARGUMENT CalculatorGraph Run failed in Run Calculator Process for node EmbeddingsCalculator failed Input length 617 longer than allowed 512 Issue submission checklist X I m reporting an issue It s not a question X I checked the problem with the documentation FAQ open issues Stack Overflow etc and have not found a solution X There is reproducer code and related data files such as images videos models etc

comments.body: fedecompa The windows version of the server was not retrieving correctly the information from the model about the context It is now corrected on the main branch Note that generative endpoint on windows server are now under development and testing Production ready windows version of the server will be published in the coming release
dtrawins thanks for the reply so to test it I need to wait for the openvino model server 2024 6 gpu right

fedecompa for the docker image and linux binary package you can use the public image 2024 5 Just follow the demo from https github com openvinotoolkit model server tree releases 2024 5 demos rerank Windows native binary package is planned to be published in 2025 0 in February It is possible though to build the windows package from sources

dtrawins no because I m using the same docker compose and the same models but with the image openvino model server 2024 5 gpu it works and with the image openvino model server 2025 0 gpu it doesn t work and throws the above error

fedecompa That is very strange Can you share the logs and output of docker inspect command for the running container Also what is the host OS and platform and GPU model Generally it is recommended to use for version 2025 0 the models exported also with OV2025 0 and the requirements from https raw githubusercontent com openvinotoolkit model server refs heads releases 2025 0 demos common export models requirements txt The error message suggest however the problem is that GPU is not working inside the container Could it that you have some very old integrated GPU which is not supported in the latest drivers https github com intel compute runtime releases tag 24 52 32224 5 which are in the latest docker image

dtrawins so I need to re export again the model with the new version of openvino Yes I updated the drivers to the latest version for windows 11 31 0 101 2134 for the Intel R UHD Graphics It is present in the list https www intel com content www us en download 776137 intel 7th 10th gen processor graphics windows html

fedecompa if you are using windows host you don t need docker containers You could just use windows native package from 2025 0 release It is recommended to reexport the models but this is not related to your error Your windows driver does support your GPU but most likely the driver in the latest public docker image doesn t If you need to use docker container you might need to build the image with older driver version or with Ubuntu22 base image

dtrawins but most likely the driver in the latest public docker image doesn t Then this means that there has been a regression in the image model server 2025 0 gpu because with the image model server 2024 5 gpu it works

fedecompa the public image includes the drivers supporting newer platforms which unfortunately drop support for the older But you can still enable version 2025 0 to work on the older machines Option1 build the image with older version git clone b releases 2025 0 https github com openvinotoolkit model server cd model server make release image INSTALL DRIVER VERSION 24 26 30049 Option2 just all the older drivers to the public image It will be quicker Build the image using the Dockerfile below FROM openvino model server 2025 0 USER 0 ENV INSTALL DRIVER VERSION 24 26 30049 RUN curl L https raw githubusercontent com openvinotoolkit model server refs heads releases 2025 0 install ubuntu gpu drivers sh o tmp install gpu drivers sh chmod 755 tmp install gpu drivers sh tmp install gpu drivers sh USER ovms ENTRYPOINT ovms bin ovms

title: Deploying YOLOv8n Model
body: Describe the bug I m trying to deploy the YOLOv8n model using OVMS The YOLO model was obtained from the example in https github com openvinotoolkit openvino notebooks blob latest notebooks yolov8 optimization yolov8 object detection ipynb I ve done a little post processing to the output tensor to obtain the classification result from the model using the jupyter notebook running on OV it seems like it s able to produce the correct result as shown below Sample post processing code image https github com user attachments assets deab4389 5077 4a94 9221 1844155a31c3 Result image https github com user attachments assets 810f2321 732b 4ec4 bcf9 596ea30cbb54 I have put the same post processing and model to OVMS but have obtained a different result image https github com user attachments assets a0b480a5 fcf1 4ab8 bed2 16826a4e2166 We should be getting at minimum class id of 16 dog From OVMS we aren t seeing dog at all Both input image is preprocessed to the model input required size of 640x640 with letterbox fill image https github com user attachments assets ff0718fa 195f 44a0 a937 ad84f49b1330 This leads me to think that there some configuration or preprocessing steps missing Does running the YOLO model on OVMS requires any other additional configuration as compared to OV other than the Tensor being named Is there similar example that I can reference YOLO if possible Snip of the model s xml image https github com user attachments assets 67338e24 bd92 487c b9ed 1250e1201135 image https github com user attachments assets 14b1dfc0 162e 4a6a be70 09eaffe73341 image https github com user attachments assets 79597fcc 727c 43dd 884b 8f43b7a401aa

title: Model server inference using Python Mediapipe
body: How can i loop over a set of detection results to run classifier over detected regions using mediapipe graph It will be helpful if i get a graph example using openvino inference calculator

comments.body: Could you share more details You mention python in the title Do you mean python mediapipe package or do you want to execute python code in mediapipe graph in OVMS I assume the flow you want to achieve would look like 1 Put image on the input of the graph 2 Run it through detection model 3 Extract detected regions and run them through classifier 4 Return some kind of combined results Is that right

mzegla Thanks for your prompt response I want to excecute python code alongwith media pipe graph I want to iterate through OVMS PY TENSOR containing detected regions inside the mediapipe graph to facilitate classification over those detected regions

Well python execution is enabled via separate node in the mediapipe graph there is a dedicated calculator for that Checkout https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main docs python support quickstart md I suppose the easiest solution would be to have your whole processing done in Python so you would have a single node that loads your detection and classification model in initialize method of OvmsPythonModel and then run detection extraction and classification in the execute method See https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main docs python support reference md Note that you will likely need to extend docker image with layers containing python packages you need like numpy opencv etc openvino is already available https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main docs python support reference md building docker image The other solution is to have multiple nodes detection extraction and classification where only extraction is done in Python and detection classification is executed via CPP based calculators This approach also requires converter nodes between nodes mentioned earlier See CLIP demo for reference https github com openvinotoolkit model server tree main demos python demos clip image classification

Hi kuaikuai Tensorflow s make tensor proto when the input array has only one value returns partial request that is currently unsupported i e python tf make tensor proto np array 0 dtype np int32 dtype DT INT32 tensor shape dim size 1 dim size 1 int val 0 as opposed to python tf make tensor proto np array 0 1 dtype np int32 dtype DT INT32 tensor shape dim size 1 dim size 2 tensor content 000 000 000 000 001 000 000 000 OVMS only parses input values located in tensor content and support for other value fields is not planned at the moment For gRPC any solution compliant with Kserve API https docs openvino ai 2024 ovms docs clients kfs html would not face this issue and it is the prefered method of communication with Model Server
why does OVMS only parse input values located in tensor content Is parsing tensor content faster than other value fields

This representation is type agnostic and reduces serialization overhead during RPC call by avoiding serialization of many repeated small items Type specific representation e g int val is slightly less performant and redundant

title: How to transfer the models in the `model zoo` to the configuration file and the pipelines?
body: I have deplyed the model server in my case it s a wonderful project I have a few questions about using the model server for the further applications I want to transfer the models from model zoo to model server s configuration file and pipelines followed the documentation https docs openvino ai 2024 ovms docs dag html there are a few samples that I have tested But how do I transfer more models How to get inputs and set outputs from the ir xml files Should I use third party tools Anyone can help me Thanks a lot

comments.body: Hi jiekechoo I think the easiest way is just to load model in OVMS and check logs on log level INFO default you should see lines like these 2024 03 18 21 53 05 366 1 modelmanager info modelinstance cpp 490 Input name input 0 mapping name input 0 shape 1 299 299 3 precision FP32 layout N 2024 03 18 21 53 05 366 1 modelmanager info modelinstance cpp 542 Output name InceptionResnetV2 AuxLogits Logits BiasAdd 0 mapping name InceptionResnetV2 AuxLogits Logits BiasAdd 0 shape 1 1001 precision FP32 layout N Alternatively you could use model metadata calls https docs openvino ai 2024 ovms docs rest api kfs html model metadata api a name model metadata a https docs openvino ai 2024 ovms docs grpc api kfs html model metadata api a name kfs model metadata a after loading those models in OVMS

atobiszei Thanks for your reply As you mentioned that was useful I can check the inputs and the outputs from the v1 or v2 rest api insted of using the DEBUG log level opts I need a documentation or a guide teach me how to create a custom pipeline for multiple models

Did you check examples https docs openvino ai 2024 ovms docs dag html pipelines examples a name pipeline examples a I don t know what specific part of custom pipeline creation is ambiguous for you so I would recommend looking at https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main docs demultiplexing md basic demultiplexer example and metadata explanation as it shows both config json and in graphic way model inputs outputs Eg Looking at this fragment name Model B node model name Model B type DL model inputs input A node name Model A node data item output A input B node name Model A node data item output B outputs data item output alias output Node representing Model B will receive output output A from node Model A node and set it as input input A to actual model This is naive example when output of one model do match exactly input of another one so you may need to use additional custom nodes to do some kind of pre post processing There are few custom nodes included in OVMS image https github com openvinotoolkit model server tree main src custom nodes

body: While sending an image inference request to ovms server receives error Processing HTTP REST request failed POST v1 models resnet50 predict Reason Could not parse input content Not valid ndarray detected

comments.body: Could you provide more details Especially 1 Logs from the model server 2 Client code that you use to send requests to the model

log from model server 2024 03 08 02 21 35 185 125 serving debug http server cpp 194 REST request v1 models resnet50 predict 2024 03 08 02 21 35 185 125 serving debug http server cpp 206 Processing HTTP request POST v1 models resnet50 predict body 9880 bytes 2024 03 08 02 21 35 185 125 serving debug http rest api handler cpp 705 Processing REST request for model resnet50 version DEFAULT 2024 03 08 02 21 35 185 125 serving debug http rest api handler cpp 714 Found model with name resnet50 Searching for requested version 2024 03 08 02 21 35 185 125 serving debug modelmanager cpp 1550 Requesting model resnet50 version 0 2024 03 08 02 21 35 186 125 serving debug model hpp 89 Getting default version for model resnet50 1 2024 03 08 02 21 35 186 125 serving debug modelinstance cpp 1031 Model resnet50 version 1 already loaded 2024 03 08 02 21 35 187 125 serving debug http server cpp 225 Processing HTTP REST request failed POST v1 models resnet50 predict Reason Could not parse instance content Not valid ndarray detected Client Writing a REST client Client log Sending POST request url is http localhost 8000 v1 models resnet50 predict Payload is instances 0 9j 4AAQSkZJRgABAQAAAQABAAD 2wCEAAkGBwgHBgkIBwgKCgkLDRYPDQw Zj04cj3x 3UE eOSnUUZ7CT xUoh 2Q Got response from 400 http localhost 8000 v1 models resnet50 predict

title: Enabling HTTPS end points on OpenVINO Model server
body: Would be great if OVMS can support HTTPS end point by being to authenticate the server as well as establish secure SSL encrypted channels to OVMS I know that you an optional NGINX front end but the problem is that communication between the NGINX and the OVMS backend is over HTTP and thus unencrypted We would like to up an Inferencing Service based on OVMS where one of the requirements is being able to maintain confidentiality of inferencing inputs We use Gramine Shielded Containers to transform the standard OVMS docker image to one that can readily run within Intel SGX and this preserve input confidentiality during execution However the service still cannot guarantee full confidentiality unless the endpoints are also secure NGINX does not solve the problem I am happy to discuss further if someone wants more information Thanks

title: [Feature Request]: Add a custom inference result handler for Model Server.
body: Request Description The custom inference result handler allows developers to directly process the result matrix in the Model Server after inference making the results more label specific This can reduce the computational load on the client side and improve development efficiency especially when the client is web based Feature Use Case Often when calling the Model Server one expects to receive directly usable result labels rather than a numerical matrix Handling numerical matrices in languages like Java is not very user friendly Moreover inference servers are typically equipped with high configurations to have sufficient performance to also handle label parsing Developing another client for this purpose would only complicate matters and is not elegant Issue submission checklist X The feature request or improvement must be related to OpenVINO

title: Custom Model Loader Timing diagrams
body: This is about the Custom Model Loader feature of the OpenVINO model server I understand the Custom Model Loader is supposed to define the functions within the CustomLoaderInterface class template however I cannot find any documentation on how when these functions are called by the OVMS model manager Without such documentation IMHO one cannot produce a meaningful implementation of the CustomLoaderInterface class From the logs of the SampleCustomLoader I see rather unintuitive behaviors such as models getting loaded even before any inference request is placed For example if the CustomLoader is configured with a config json file that contains multiple models the custom loader attempts to pre load all the models even before any of these models are called for inference Also what is the difference between unload and retire models When do these get called After every inference It would be very helpful to obtain timing diagrams that describe usage of custom model loader functions by model manager Thanks

comments.body: From the logs of the SampleCustomLoader I see rather unintuitive behaviors such as models getting loaded even before any inference request is placed For example if the CustomLoader is configured with a config json file that contains multiple models the custom loader attempts to pre load all the models even before any of these models are called for inference This is designed behavior models are not lazy initialized but are loaded beforehand and ready for inference Also what is the difference between unload and retire models When do these get called After every inference Basically none I believe unfortunately the API function names were named differently for very similar operations unloadModel modelName version unloads retires specific model version retireModel modelName should perform the same but for all model versions I think OVMS behavior should be changed here and only use unloadModel and not care about the others Otherwise it basically tries to unload model version twice when using custom loader Basically OVMS model could be in following stages BEGIN beginning of model existence even backend load operation didn t start LOADING LOADING ERROR AVAILABLE this means that model is loaded and ready for operation UNLOADING UNLOADING ERROR END this means that model is unloaded retired Cannot be used Some configuration changes may require partial model reload however assumption is that since we don t know anything about specific custom loader we do full model reload in such cases that is we unload model and then load it again Hope it helps until we improve the documentation
If there is no response the topic will be closed within a week

title: OVMS performance in CPU
body: I have a setup where I am serving 5 models and number of requests per second is quite high Here are few things I am trying to understand As explained in the throughput related section https docs openvino ai latest openvino docs deployment optimization guide tput html doxid openvino docs deployment optimization guide tput the OpenVINO streams is a mean of running multiple requests in parallel In order to best serve multiple inference requests executed simultaneously the inference threads are grouped pinned to the particular CPU cores constituting the CPU streams This provides much better performance for the networks than batching especially for the many core machines Is inference thread is different from threading in general concept of programming For setting optimal CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS can total number of streams from all model be larger than number NO CPU CORE For example CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS for all models has been set to NO CPU CORE

comments.body: m bulbul The concept of inference threads is the same Inference execution initiates multiple threads to take advantage of execution concurrency and multi core CPUs By default OpenVINO is consuming all the cores with the same number of threads Some models however can not efficiently utilized all cores while some branches of the model topology are executed in sequences That is observed especially on HW with very high number of cores STREAMS address this challenge by executing multiple inference requests in parallel Each stream is using a part of the overall capacity which makes the concurrency more efficient Increasing the number of streams often improves the throughput when there are multiple inference executions in parallel It is not recommended to set the number of streams higher from the number of cores The optimal number of streams might depend on the model HW capacity expected latency and the number of parallel inference requests It is possible to use also a simplified approach with setting just the PERFORMANCE HINT parameter to LATENCY or THROUGHPUT You can learn more about the performance aspect of streams on https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main docs python benchmarking client 16feb pdf
Thanks for the input That helped

Hi dtrawins I have few more questions Here is my understanding LATENCY mode is preferred for single inference and in LATENCY mode all the core and threads are used for the inference Cores are evenly distributed among STREAMS so when CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS is set 1 it should perform similar to LATENCY mode for a single model Now for multiple models say two since two different model often has different architecture and will take different time for inference how to distribute core accordingly say model A 60 model B 40 Can we achieve something like this in ovms I m guessing it s through CPU THREADS NUM In THROUGHPUT mode ovms dynamically divides the resources based on the available resources is it possible to know how many streams each models have been assigned

m bulbul your understanding for LATENCY mode is correct It has similar behavior like a single stream CPU THREADS NUM can limit the number of cores to be consumed by a single model That way you could reserve certain resources for the model In can each model is used sporadically it will be still ok to assign all resources for each model They can be used concurrently using the same resources Limiting the threads might be recommended if you need to guarantee the response time regardless of the load on the other model OVMS is reporting in the logs the number of inference requests creating while loading the model When nireq parameter is not set the number of inference requests in the logs is equal to the number of streams

title: Question
body: With the quick start guide I am able to add my own client to this model How Can I modify the server model to customize

comments.body: Shwetaspc Hi can you provide more details what modifications you would like to make
I want to modify proto files and define custom GRPC API s Ex We already have predict GRPC API for face detection module Similary I want to add few GRPC API s for my social distancing module

Well you will need to look deeply at the flows in the model server to see exactly what you need to modify to add custom API You could add a service with your custom API here https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main src server cpp L194 L195 If you choose to modify or base on existing PredictionService you would need to adjust it to work with your custom objects for requests and responses https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main src prediction service cpp L65 If you look at the implementation of this service you can see that data in the request is used both for getting the right model and running prediction so your request need to contain data as well as information about the model model name and model version In other methods you will need to extract it and use it to get the right ModelInstance For simple inference you will need to make infer method work with your API https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main src modelinstance cpp L994 That includes changing request validation deserialization and serialization Adding custom API or modifying existing is quite a big task so make sure you understand how the model server works internally before making changes if you want to use your customized version in production environment

Shwetaspc Why the API changes are needed Perhaps you have in mind just using different model with different input and outputs For that there is not need to change the API and proto definition It is generic so it can support arbitrary model and use case

title: use model server gRPC api from gstreamer pipeline
body: I want to call model server gRPC api from sink or src pad of some gstreamer pipeline element pad add probe Gst PadProbeType BUFFER pad probe callback frame VideoFrame buffer caps caps how can I prepare request img data from frame data request predict pb2 PredictRequest request inputs data CopyFrom make tensor proto img shape img shape

comments.body: I believe that s right If frame data is a numpy array then it can be used similar to what you wrote request predict pb2 PredictRequest request inputs data CopyFrom make tensor proto img shape img shape Keep in mind that the request you send must match the model you use So if your frame is 512x512 and the model accepts images of size 300x300 then you might need to resize it before sending to OVMS Also most models that process images have certain layout defined NHWC NCHW where N batch size C color channels H image height W image width So your model might take inputs of shape 1 3 300 300 The frame you have might have different layout 1 300 300 3 or might not contain batch size dimension 3 300 300 Before creating the request make sure the numpy array you have matches the model input

title: ovms async/sync model
body: I use openvino benchmark tools and I found I can use api async sync but ovms I can not found this option ovms does not support it the default is to use async

comments.body: The openvino benchmark app works in a manner similar to this Loop 1 Schedule async inference on N data chunk 2 Read results for N 1 data chunk OVMS does not have a context of many data chunks in one thread it receives requests one by one on each server thread Internally OVMS uses async inference but it s not exposed to the user as there s only one way model server can process incoming requests
thank you very much

title: Need of  Understanding of Demultiplexer workflow
body: Hi In a project of Analysis of multiple faces in single image frame request I want to understand the workflow of demultiplexer It looks a little bit confusing Because I am learning After detecting the face images in this below input There are total 10 face images in the below input so demultiplexer creates a total of 10 requests with the shape Note I had changed demultiply count from 0 to 10 in config JSON file for better understanding of shapes of input and output of a node It does works after change to 10 My question is After completion of face detection node and the custom node we are resizing the face Image to the shape of 10 1 64 64 3 and this shape is the input for the next two models age and emotion recognition How does it splits the requests to the next two models Because both models are using same inputs as 10 1 64 64 3 I am a very confused at this stage It does splits 5 requests to each model or it splits 10 to each model Looking for response people1 https user images githubusercontent com 57169077 125195711 79a6f280 e274 11eb 8aaf 8891608d597b jpeg Thanks

comments.body: Hi bhargav sudo Note I had changed demultiply count from 0 to 10 in config JSON file for better understanding of shapes of input and output of a node It does works after change to 10 Yes that change works but only if you sent images that detect exactly 10 faces If you will be sending images that will have varied number of detections you need to set demultiply count 0 After completion of face detection node and the custom node we are resizing the face Image to the shape of 10 1 64 64 3 and this shape is the input for the next two models age and emotion recognition How does it splits the requests to the next two models Because both models are using same inputs as 10 1 64 64 3 I am a very confused at this stage It does splits 5 requests to each model or it splits 10 to each model Custom node prepares the output in the shape detectionCount 1 64 64 3 Then when pipeline receives such output demultiplexer divides it into 10 requests for following nodes with shape 1 64 64 3 Each of following nodes receives each cropped face image Then at the gathering node exit node if not specified it will gather the results from the previous demultiplication So in the case of face coordinates output it will merge 10x 1 4 into 10 1 4

title: Graceful shutdown - GRPC port stays in use
body: Hi when doing stress test on OVMS server we have found some cases where the GRPC port is still being allocated even after killing the OVMS process sometimes for 30s 1min Is it a known behavior Is there a way to force port to get cleaned when shutting down the process with a kill signal in Unix Thanks

comments.body: Hi do you kill OVMS when it s still processing requests If so then to me it looks like expected behavior The client server connection is not freed immediately after one of the sides wants to finish it and the TCP connection is still on for a while to prevent delayed requests from being received by the next application that uses the same port That s why sometimes server might occupy the port for a bit longer to make sure everything is closed properly before freeing it We don t modify that behavior in our tests but I found something like this On Linux systems the TIMED WAIT state is a kernel value tcp sys net ipv4 tcp fin timeout is where this kernel value is stored To update the current setting echo 30 proc sys net ipv4 tcp fin timeout To view the current setting cat proc sys net ipv4 tcp fin timeout So you can try that it might require rebuilding docker image with such modification in place but I have no idea if this will work for you

comments.body: Hi Yes number provided in nireq parameter determines how many inferences can be scheduled on the device at the same time Model server internally schedules asynchronous inference for every request no matter what device you are using Although to have multiple inferences performed in parallel you need to send multiple requests in parallel You can do this either by using multiple threads to send requests or by sending requests in asynchronous manner
Okay thanks for clarifying

title: Dynamic Batch Size and Shape in DAG Pipelines
body: Hi I have managed to implement a pipeline with a custom node that takes results from a face detection model and transforms the results into something an emotion detection model can use which is great I really like this feature My current client code uses batching to get more performance out of the model server and I am trying to replicate this inside the pipeline with no success so far For example I would want to send 4 images into the pipeline where the custom node would use the face detection results for each image to then output all of the faces detected across all of the images into the emotion detection model I have not managed to get this working using a fixed nor dynamic batch size My first question is is the above example possible If so how can I adjust the batch size or shape of the face detection model if the DAG pipeline limits batch size when using demultiplexer nodes My current model server config which works well with a single input image is model config list config name face detection retail 0004 base path opt test face detection retail 0004 config name emotions recognition retail 0003 base path opt test emotions recognition retail 0003 shape 1 3 64 64 custom node library config list name andyTestNode base path opt test lib libcustom node andyTest so pipeline config list name fullFace inputs image fullSizeImage nodes name faceDetection model name face detection retail 0004 version 2 type DL model inputs data node name request data item image outputs data item detection out alias faceDetections name customNode library name andyTestNode type custom demultiply count 0 params original image width 640 original image height 480 target image width 64 target image height 64 debug true imOutputDir home ovms inputs image node name request data item image faceDetections node name faceDetection data item faceDetections fullSizeImage node name request data item fullSizeImage outputs data item faceImages alias faces data item formattedFaceDetections alias faceDetections name emotions model name emotions recognition retail 0003 type DL model inputs data node name customNode data item faces outputs data item prob emotion alias emotion outputs boundingBoxes node name customNode data item faceDetections faces node name customNode data item faces emotion node name emotions data item emotion Trying to change the batch size or shape of the face detection model produces errors adding shape auto gives a shape forbidden error and adding shape 2 3 300 300 gives the error modelmanager error pipelinedefinition cpp 361 Pipeline fullFace node faceDetection inputName data inputShape 2 3 300 300 Batch size 2 is not allowed for non gathering nodes Any help on how to set up the model server config would be appreciated Andy

comments.body: Hi We are happy with your positive feedback I would want to send 4 images into the pipeline where the custom node would use the face detection results for each image to then output all of the faces detected across all of the images into the emotion detection model I have not managed to get this working using a fixed nor dynamic batch size My first question is is the above example possible There is no possibility to change batch size to 2 if you use demultiplexer Sending batch size 1 could be impractical since you could have different number of faces detected on each image Then the DAG would have to pack those which creates ambiguity how the output shape would look like since you should still be able to know from which image your detection was If so how can I adjust the batch size or shape of the face detection model if the DAG pipeline limits batch size when using demultiplexer nodes You can edit the shape just keep batch size equal 1 shape 1 3 300 300 If you are working on improving performance you could try sending multiple requests with batch 1 simultaneously changing CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS or and nireq configuration per model it may be called DEVICE TYPE THROUGHPUT STREAMS depends on hardware on which you run inference So for example for face detection model you would change config to something like this config name face detection retail 0004 base path opt test face detection retail 0004 plugin config CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS 4 nireq 16 What the values should be is dependent on hardware used I gave 4 16 as an example here If we would have more details about the use case then we could advise more With current information we think that sending multiple requests simultaneously is the best path here Adrian

Hi Thanks for the response I have a couple of questions regarding using asynchronous call with the model server I have used the CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS and nireq properties before so I recognise the example config you posted Does this mean that setting the model to handle async requests will allow the pipeline to handle async requests Meaning I don t need to add anything to the pipeline config list property Also would I need to set these two properties for each model in the pipeline or just the entry node for the pipeline Andy

Hi Does this mean that setting the model to handle async requests will allow the pipeline to handle async requests All predict requests calls to OVMS are blocking client need to wait for response but the predictions themselves are running in parallel CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS is defining how many parallel inferences is happening nireq is defining how many parallel predictions can be prepared for execution Pipelines use the same CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS nireq pool to execute inferences but each inference in pipeline can occur simultaneously if it has required inputs ready Meaning I don t need to add anything to the pipeline config list property You don t have to add anything to pipeline config list Both parameters are for model configuration Also would I need to set these two properties for each model in the pipeline or just the entry node for the pipeline You need to define those parameters for all models used in pipeline Up to some point higher throughput streams means that you can process more inferences at a time so it increases throughput at the cost of latency Default values for those parameters are compromise but you can optimize towards one or the other Adrian
Hi Thanks for clarifying that it was very helpful Andy
Steedance Let us know if you need more information or we can close this issue

title: If I modify the sever source code, how should i compile it ?
body: excuse me if i modify the sever source code how should I compile it Can you provide some tutorials such as a build sh file

comments.body: Hi There are steps to compile OVMS in Docker https github com openvinotoolkit model server blob main docs developer guide md step 1 compile source code After running make docker build a openvino model server build latest image is created It s quite big but contains all dependencies needed to build model server so you can simply mount OVMS source code and run bazel build src ovms to compile
mzegla thanks I have another question when use docker pull openvino model server latest the docker just have 441M may be have some errors docker run it xxx can t be work

That s right It s because the published image is meant to be as light as possible It contains only what s necessary to run model server so the stuff required to compile OVMS is not there To have the image that you could get into and recompile sources you need to build the image yourself Running make docker build produces a bunch of images One of them is openvino model server build latest which you can use to modify model server code and recompile it
mzegla thanks make docker build Where is this order executed need to execute after entering docker i don t how to run this order

You execute this command on your host machine 1 Clone model server repository with git clone 2 Get into model server root directory 3 Run make docker build 4 When your images are built run docker run it v PWD ovms entrypoint bash p 9178 9178 openvino model server build latest start container with interactive bash shell 5 Now that you re in the container you can change source code source code is mounted in the container so you can do that in the IDE on the host and then from the container bash shell you can run bazel build src ovms

mzegla thanks I still have some questions Do I follow the steps below in host i don t have environment 1 docker pull openvino model server latest 2 docker run it openvino model server latest 3 sudo docker attach openvino model server latest then follow 4 Clone model server repository with git clone 5 Get into model server root directory 6 Run make docker build

The pulling is not necessary You don t need openvino model server latest You should clone repo to your machine not into docker container and run make docker build directly on you machine It will build a bunch of images and when you have them once make docker build finishes successfully you can go with docker run on openvino model server build latest make docker build does not simply compiles OVMS It creates docker images like the one you would pull from dockerhub One of these images is openvino model server build latest which contains dependencies and packages needed to rebuild model server When you have that image you can mount the source code to the container and after modifications in the code run bazel build like I mentioned earlier 4 When your images are built run docker run it v PWD ovms entrypoint bash p 9178 9178 openvino model server build latest start container with interactive bash shell 5 Now that you re in the container you can change source code source code is mounted in the container so you can do that in the IDE on the host and then from the container bash shell you can run bazel build src ovms
mzegla thank you very much very good
You re welcome

It seems correct that when using command without parameters you get better performance Looking at the way you send requests it seems it s the best configuration Without parameters OVMS starts with one server thread and one CPU Stream and that s all you can utilize simply using single face detection py client It s because face detection py sends requests synchronously so OVMS cannot process for example 2 images at the same time because it gets requests one by one So even though you specified grpc workers nireq and CPU streams numer to be more than 1 your client doesn t take advantage of it and you end up with even worse performance than when you run model server with single thread and CPU Stream Either way OpenVINO uses only physical cores and from my experience it divides physical cores into streams of 4 so I would say for your setup 1 stream is optimal and setting this numer to higher you set 5 will be nonoptimal To me it looks like setting plugin config causes performance difference between the two variants you posted I would recommend using default plugin config modifying client application to send multiple requests at a time in multiple threads or processes setting grpc workers and nireq to numer at least as big as number of requests senders from previous point You can also see what is max performance your setup can get by using desired model directly with OpenVINO for example with benchmark app https docs openvinotoolkit org latest inference engine tools benchmark tool README html

Ok so from my understanding CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS specifies number of streams i e groups of cores that would separately handle inference requests So if you have 16 cores and 2 streams then you re able to perform 2 inferences in parallel first 8 cores will handle first request next 8 cores will handle second request Normally if you don t set CPU THORUGHPUT STREAMS you get one stream and all cores are handling one request so requests are handled in sequence one by one When you have a lot of cores then using all of them to handle the same request is not very effective unless you only care about latency so to achieve better throughput with such CPUs you can split cores into groups streams and make each of them handle its own request This way you can effectively do multiple inferences at the same time If you decide to use multiple streams make sure nireq is more or equal to the number of streams For your use case I encourage you to try with default settings 1 stream because to me it looks like you ll have trouble with providing enough data to the model to make multiple streams approach effective From what I ve observed when model does not get enough data using multiple streams performs worse than using single one This drop in performance for batch size bigger than 4 might be caused by using 8 cpu streams Please try with default plugin config 1 stream and let me know about the findings

Thanks mzegla Apologies a few more questions based on what you have said here but it s very useful for my understanding So the way that you talk it sounds that the stream almost reserves CPU threads for use If that is the case then using the multiple model configuration from my initial comment here how would it behave if we were making requests for different models in parallel For example sending 8 requests to person and face detection in parallel Would they fight for CPU threads Would it be better to reserve a subset of the total threads for each function e g person plugin config CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS 4 CPU THREADS NUM 16 face plugin config CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS 4 CPU THREADS NUM 16 as opposed to always specifying the max threads 32 Also why do you think that I will struggle to get data to my server The code above is just a small testing piece but we are aiming for max throughput against model server here so if there s anything I might be missing then I would love to know We are processing many many more images than the test script above w r t your final comment I ran a small number of tests on the benchmarking tool using command benchmark app py m opt intel openvino deployment tools open model zoo tools downloader intel person detection retail 0013 FP32 person detection retail 0013 xml nstreams 1 t 30 image https user images githubusercontent com 45638338 82221412 e1370b80 9917 11ea 8037 468e4e938c8e png

I m not sure but I believe that it s not exactly that certain model reserves some number of cores From my experience it looks more like they re assigned dynamically I haven t tested OVMS that way with multiple models using multiple streams but I think that your example person plugin config CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS 4 CPU THREADS NUM 16 face plugin config CPU THROUGHPUT STREAMS 4 CPU THREADS NUM 16 Would result in each model using at most 25 of all cores and that would mean you ll be having 4 streams for those two models not 8 4 per one I think this plugin config takes into account all cores for each model That s my understanding but as I mentioned I have not tested it myself so I might be wrong About providing enough data to the server It all depends Depends on the model input size etc OVMS does not always reproduce OpenVINO performance especially for high throughput use cases Model server itself can be incapable of handling certain amount of requests What I mean by that is that OV might be able to perform more inferences than OVMS can process at a time You don t see that problem when using benchmarking app OV directly and locally And for the amount of requests when model server starts to be the bottleneck using multiple streams might be not that effective Could you compare the results running tests on OVMS rather than OpenVINO and see if it still is better with multiple streams Because maybe for your model it s okay Well it seems that even benchmarking app reports worse performance for bigger batch sizes so it might be natural for that model
Hi Apologies for the late response I managed to get an increased performance by using multiple clients so thanks for all of the help and information

title: Dynamically change configuration file
body: How can we dynamically add or delete new models without restarting the service

comments.body: Hi Once you start a service with desired models you won t be able to add or delete models without restarting a service Models paths and version policies set at the beginning and cannot be changed after server starts The only way to change what s served is with model versions For example if you have a model in opt model with version 1 i e opt model 1 then you can place another model in let s say opt model 2 In this situation depending on that model s version policy you can have both versions served for model version policy all only version 2 for model version policy latest Server detects adding and removing versions and updates to match model version policy For more details on model version policy check out https github com IntelAI OpenVINO model server blob master docs docker container md model version policy

golisandeep3 The functionality for adding or removing the models is now added to new OVMS version 2021 1 With this new release you can just edit the config file OVMS will detect the changes and apply the needed updates without restarting the service and impacting its availability
